newsitem.title: ALBANIA: As politicians haggle, Albanians seek normality.
newsitem.headline: As politicians haggle, Albanians seek normality.

text.p: As Albania's politicians haggled over a new electoral law on Sunday, thousands of ordinary people took to the streets to relax and try to forget the riots and fighting that have brought near anarchy to their country.
Old and young strolled and chatted in an almost carnival atmosphere as they took advantage of one of the first hot days of summer and tried to get back to some normality.
But armed men in civilian clothes outside the office of President Sali Berisha and the armoured cars of Western troops were a sharp reminder of the recent chaos.
Despite calm in the capital, other parts of Europe's poorest nation still saw sporadic outbreaks of the violence that has shaken Albania in the past three months.

"It is so nice that today we are out to forget everything and to put it far away," said Mimosa Pushani, out walking with her two young childen and husband along the banks of a lake near one of the Albanian capital's parks.
Albania was shaken by rioting in February and March after tens of thousands of people lost their life savings when a string of high-yield-high-risk pyramid investment schemes collapsed.

General lawlessness swept the south of the country as gangs demanding the ouster of Berisha and armed with weapons looted from abandoned police and army depots seized control of towns and villages Although Tirana saw far less violence than the south, a curfew is still in force from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
Western soldiers are everywhere, part of a 6,000-strong, U.N.-backed force whose mandate is to protect humanitarian aid supplies.

As ordinary people tried to forget their problems, political parties were meeting European election experts to finalise a new electoral law to enable new elections to take place as planned on June 29.
The 10 main parties on Friday signed a six-point political contract with European envoy Franz Vranitzky, committing them to a vote on the new law by Monday.
In the rest of Albania, outbreaks of lawlessness continue.

The state-run news agency ATA reported on Saturday that two people were killed in a gun battle in the southern port Vlore and a 13-year-old girl was wounded by robbers targetting Albanians travelling to and from Greece.
